market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by 4–8%?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

The all-time series is tied 24-24. The most recent meeting was a 16-13 Texans win in November 2025.
Friday's final practice report with game designations comes before Sunday's 1:00 PM ET kickoff (12:00 PM CT). Anderson's, Simmons's and Hooker's statuses were still unresolved as of Thursday.

market.question: Will the Tampa Bay Rays win the 2026 World Series?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2026 MLB World Series. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2026 MLB World Series per the rules of MLB (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 MLB season is cancelled, postponed after December 31, 2026 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from MLB (https://www.mlb.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: The Dodgers beat the Braves 3-1 in the 2026 NLDS. They won Game 1 5-3, lost Game 2 2-3, won Game 3 3-1 and closed out the series with a 4-1 win in Game 4 at Truist Park on Oct. 7.

In the NLCS, the No. 1 seed Brewers, who had the best record in baseball, play the No. 2 seed Dodgers, with Milwaukee holding home field. Games 1-2 are Oct. 11-12 in Milwaukee and Games 3-5 are Oct. 14-16 in Los Angeles (Game 5 if necessary). Games 6-7, if necessary, are Oct. 18-19 in Milwaukee.
The Brewers won the 2026 regular-season series against the Dodgers 4-3. The Dodgers have won all three previous postseason meetings between the clubs (2018 NLCS, 2020 Wild Card Series, 2025 NLCS).
MLB.com calls the Dodgers the two-time reigning World Series champions (2024 and 2025).

The White Sox led the ALDS against the Guardians 2-1 going into Game 4 at Rate Field on Thursday, Oct. 8, 8 p.m. ET. A Cleveland win would force Game 5. I could not find a final score for Game 4 in any source as of this research.
The Guardians beat the White Sox 9-3 in ALDS Game 3 at Rate Field, ending Chicago's 4-0 start to the postseason. The White Sox had won Game 1 in Cleveland and Game 2 4-3 on Oct. 5.
If needed, ALDS Game 5 between the Guardians and White Sox is Saturday, Oct. 10, at 8 p.m. ET at Progressive Field in Cleveland.

The Rays swept the Yankees 3-0 in their ALDS and will host the winner of Guardians vs. White Sox in the ALCS. Games 1-2 are Oct. 12-13 at Tampa Bay, Games 3-4 are Oct. 15-16, and Games 5-7, if needed, are Oct. 17, 19 and 20.

The White Sox finished the regular season 84-78, one game behind the Guardians for the AL Central title. They swept the AL West champion Astros 2-0 in the Wild Card Series, winning the clincher 7-3 in Houston.

Postseason results so far: in the Wild Card round, the White Sox beat the Astros, the Yankees beat the Red Sox, the Padres beat the Cubs and the Braves beat the Phillies. In the Division Series, the Dodgers beat the Braves 3-1, the Brewers beat the Padres and the Rays beat the Yankees 3-0. CBS lists the Brewers-Padres series as 2-1, which looks off for a best-of-five.

The 2026 World Series runs Fri. Oct. 23 (Game 1), Sat. Oct. 24, Mon. Oct. 26 and Tue. Oct. 27. If necessary, Game 5 is Wed. Oct. 28, Game 6 is Fri. Oct. 30 and Game 7 is Sat. Oct. 31. The schedule has no flexible dates.

The World Series is a best-of-seven in a 2-3-2 format, and the team with the better regular-season record hosts Games 1-2 and 6-7. A Game 7 on Oct. 31 played at night in the US would likely end after the questions' 2026-10-31T23:55Z close time.
A trip to the ALCS would be Chicago's first since 2005, the year the White Sox last won the World Series. Their 2026 postseason berth is their first since 2021.

market.question: Open de España presented by Madrid: Grant Forrest wins
market.rules:
If Grant Forrest wins the Open de España presented by Madrid, then the market resolves to Yes.
If a golfer forfeits, withdraws, or does not participate prior to teeing off, their contracts will resolve as follows:
Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

Ayora tees off at 13:50 Spanish time on Friday 9 October from the 1st tee, playing with Ludvig Åberg and Tyrrell Hatton. In round 1, Åberg shot even par and Hatton +5. The tournament has four rounds, 8–11 October, so it finishes Sunday 11 October.

Before the event, Jon Rahm (world #15) was listed as the highest-ranked player in the field, which also included Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Ludvig Åberg, Tyrrell Hatton, Patrick Reed and defending champion Marco Penge (#53).
Spanish opening-day reports say Jon Rahm did not play because of the birth of his fourth child. Defending champion Marco Penge and Patrick Reed both opened at +2.

Ayora (born 2004) turned pro in 2023. His only professional win is the 2024 Rosa Challenge Tour event. On the DP World Tour he has no wins; his best finishes include T7 at the 2025 Italian Open (he led outright after 36 holes) and T8 at the 2025 DP World Tour Championship. He had ten top-10s in 2025. A single Challenge Tour win is weak evidence of an ability to close out a win.

In the 2026 season (as of July), Ayora had five DP World Tour top-10s, including T5 at the Qatar Masters, T3 at the KLM Open in June and solo 5th at the Open d'Italia in late June. He missed the cut at the Scottish Open, the PGA Championship and The Open, and was 22nd in the Race to Dubai at the time of The Open.
An undated PGA Tour profile gives Ayora's Official World Golf Ranking as 121. This figure may be out of date.
Ayora finished 9th at the 2025 Open de España at the same venue (Club de Campo Villa de Madrid). He is in his second DP World Tour season and has turned down LIV Golf offers.
The question resolves Yes only if Ayora wins the tournament. If he withdraws or does not tee off, the Tournament Winner market resolves No.

recent_facts.fact: Texas vs Oklahoma (Red River Rivalry) is set for Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 3:30 PM ET (2:30 PM CDT) at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas, on ABC. The site is neutral.
No. 1 Texas is 4-0 (1-0 SEC). Results: beat Texas State 59-7, Ohio State 24-23, UTSA 30-6 and Tennessee 20-17 on the road. Two of the four wins were by 3 points or fewer.

Oklahoma is 2-2 (0-1 SEC) after losing 41-13 at Georgia on Sept 26. John Mateer had three first-half turnovers in that game (two lost fumbles and an interception) and went 25 of 34 for 231 yards, 2 TD and 1 INT.

Oklahoma's other 2026 results: beat UTEP 51-0 on Sept 4, lost 17-10 at No. 19 Michigan on Sept 12 (score from one source; unverified), and beat New Mexico only 14-6 at home on Sept 19. The Sooners had a bye before the Texas game.

In the 21 regular-season meetings from 2005 to 2025, Texas won by 8 or more points 7 times: 2005 (45-12), 2006 (28-10), 2008 (45-35), 2013 (36-20), 2022 (49-0), 2024 (34-3) and 2025 (23-6). Texas won by 7 or fewer 3 times (2009 16-13, 2015 24-17, 2018 48-45), and Oklahoma won the other 11.
Texas won 3 of the last 4 meetings, each by 17 or more points: 49-0 in 2022, 34-3 in 2024 and 23-6 in 2025. Oklahoma won 34-30 in 2023. Texas leads the all-time series 65-51-5.

Oklahoma's availability report lists 13 players: 5 out (Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton), 2 doubtful (LT Michael Fasusi, Trynae Washington), 1 questionable (Eddy Pierre-Louis) and 5 probable.

Texas's report has 4 names: OL Jordan Coleman out, WR Kaliq Lockett out, DL Zion Williams out, and DL Justus Terry questionable (has not played since Week 1). RB Hollywood Smothers, who missed the Tennessee game with a leg injury, has been cleared.
Through four games Oklahoma's offensive line has allowed 44 pressures and 9 sacks. Mateer is completing 66.1% of his passes with 8 TD and 4 INT.
Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons had 5 to 5.5 sacks in the 20-17 win at Tennessee. In that game Arch Manning went 14 of 19 for 201 yards with no TD and no INT.

recent_facts.fact: After 5 matchweeks, Arsenal were 2nd on 12 points (4 wins, 1 loss; 8 scored, 4 conceded) and Leeds were 5th on 9 points. Manchester City led on 15. Some other table snapshots were out of date.

Arsenal's last match before the international break was a 3-0 away loss to Brighton. It was their first defeat of the season, ended a seven-game winning run and was their heaviest defeat since May 2023. Earlier this season they beat Coventry 3-0 at home and Chelsea 2-1 at home.

Leeds are unbeaten in their first 5 league matches (2 wins, 3 draws) but have scored only 3 league goals, according to Opta. Their last game was a 0-0 home draw with Crystal Palace. Football Web Pages' table instead lists Leeds with 7 goals scored and 3 conceded, so the goal count is disputed.

Arsenal have won 9 of their last 10 Premier League meetings with Leeds (1 draw), including each of the last 7 by an aggregate of 24-5. Leeds have not won at Arsenal since a 3-2 win in May 2003, and Arteta is 4 wins from 4 Premier League games against Daniel Farke.
Arsenal scored at least 4 goals in both Premier League meetings with Leeds last season, and Leeds failed to score in either game. A Blick headline records one of those games as Arsenal 4-1 Leeds.
Since the start of 2024, Arsenal have lost back-to-back Premier League games only once, in April 2026.

market.question: Will Student List – Students Win win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia, Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
recent_facts.fact: An earlier Faktor Plus poll (about 4 Sept 2026, n=1,200) had the SNS-led list at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%. About one in three voters was undecided. Opposition and independent media accuse Faktor Plus and Ipsos of pro-government bias.

recent_facts.source: bne IntelliNews (CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab)
recent_facts.fact: A CRTA/Stanford DAL poll (June 2026 fieldwork) found 44.9% of decided voters backing the Student List versus 35.7% for SNS. It was reported as the first regular national poll since July 2010 to place a party other than SNS first.

Searches as of early October 2026 found no poll with October fieldwork. The latest published figures are still the late-September Faktor Plus and NSPM releases, and Vukadinović said a new NSPM poll could come out in early or mid-October.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list PR in a single nationwide constituency using D'Hondt. The threshold is 3% of votes cast, and minority lists are exempt. On the ballot, list 1 is 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS, PUPS, SPS-excluded allies, SRS and others) and list 3 is 'Student List – Students Are Winning'. SPS runs separately as list 2 ('Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability!').

DS, the Green–Left Front, PSG (which left European Serbia), POKS, SPO, Kreni-Promeni, SDS, LSV, Dveri and Enough is Enough are not running their own lists and are backing the Student List. The People's Serbia coalition (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew its list on 22 Sept to back the Student List.

The opposition vote is still split among several separate lists: European Serbia (SSP, SRCE, Solidarity), Authentic Right/NADA (NDSS, Monarchists), and Alternative for Serbia. NADA said NDSS would join a Student List-led government if it crosses the threshold.

Vučić dissolved the Assembly on 9 Sept 2026 and resigned the presidency on 27 Sept to head the SNS list as its prime ministerial candidate. The Student List is led by Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist.

The list 'Izbor naroda' withdrew after endorsing the Student List. Vreme reported that Nestorović's list, which Vukadinović said could have passed the threshold, also exited. RIK had to publish the final summary list by 9 October.

Election day is 25 Oct 2026, with polls open 07:00–20:00 and campaign silence starting two days before. Televised debates ran from 24 Sept to 9 Oct. The Student List has called on citizens to take to the streets after polls close.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia, Opinion polling for the 2023 Serbian parliamentary election
recent_facts.fact: In the December 2023 election, the SNS list got about 46.7–48.0% (129 seats) and the opposition SPN got about 23.6–24.3% (65 seats). The final NSPM poll (12 Dec, 39.8 vs 25.6) and OFID poll (38.7 vs 27.1) underestimated SNS by roughly 8–9 points. Ipsos (44.6 vs 23.6) was closest.

SNS-led lists have won the most seats in every Serbian parliamentary election since 2012: 2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022 and 2023, which is 6 of 6 (count recalled, unverified per election). The 2023 vote was marred by monitor-reported irregularities.

Observers describe Serbian elections as run under unfair conditions, including media dominance by the ruling party. Separately, pro-government tabloids have run campaigns against Srdanović using AI-manipulated photos, according to fact-checkers.
An earlier CRTA telephone poll (13–27 Sept 2025, n=2,020) found 44% support for a student list versus 32% for Vučić's bloc. This is older trend context from before the 2026 lists were formed.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Ohio Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 Ohio U.S. Senate special election currently scheduled for November 3, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: The RCP polling average for September 1 to October 5, 2026 has Democrat Sherrod Brown at 47.5% and Republican Sen. Jon Husted at 44.0%, which is Brown +3.5.
A CNN poll of 760 registered voters (Sept 29–Oct 5, MoE ±4.5) had Brown at 49% and Husted at 43%.
The Suffolk/USA Today Ohio poll had Brown at 47% and Husted at 44%, with 6% undecided. The ballot also listed Libertarian William Redpath and No Party candidate Greg Levy.

Marist surveyed 1,298 Ohio registered voters (Sept 24–27, MoE ±3.8). Brown led Husted 51% to 43%, and independents favored Brown 58% to 33%. In the governor's race, Democrat Acton led Republican Ramaswamy 50% to 44%.

Some recent polls show a closer race. InsiderAdvantage (Sept 28–29) had Brown 44%, Husted 43%. Quantus Insights (Sept 21–23) had Brown 48%, Husted 47%. Rasmussen (likely voters) had Brown 46%, Husted 43%, with 7% undecided.
A Portage County bellwether poll (MoE ±5.6) had Husted ahead of Brown 48% to 44%, unlike the statewide polls.

In the 2024 Ohio Senate race, Republican Bernie Moreno beat Brown 50.1% to 46.5% (R+3.6). The final RCP average (Oct 23–Nov 4) was Moreno +1.7, so the polls understated the Republican margin by about 1.9 points. A NYT/Siena poll in late September 2024 had Brown +4.

In 2024, Brown led in several mid-campaign polls, and the race moved toward the Republican over the last weeks. Final individual polls ranged from a tie (Trafalgar) to Moreno +3 (Emerson, AtlasIntel).
NPR calls the race a toss-up that could decide Senate control for Trump's last two years in office. Cook Political Report also rates it a Toss-up.

Brown voted in Franklin County on the first day of early voting. He pointed to voter unhappiness over the war with Iran and over food and diesel prices. Husted has said he would back a federal gas tax holiday.
The Hill reported that Donald Trump is scheduled to hold a rally for Jon Husted in Ohio.

Brown's campaign says national Republicans are spending more than $270 million against him; this is the campaign's own figure. Separately, the crypto super PAC Fairshake reportedly plans to spend at least $30 million opposing Brown.
Ohio early voting runs from Oct 6 to Nov 1, 2026, and the voter registration deadline was Oct 5. The special election is Nov 3, 2026. The searches turned up no scheduled Brown–Husted debate.
Brown raised $7.3M in Q4 2025 and had about $9.9M cash on hand. Husted's two committees raised $1.5M in Q4 and $7.3M across all of 2025.

market.question: US-Iran Hormuz Agreement by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by less than 4%?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

market.question: Will the rate of core CPI inflation be above 2.4% for the year ending in September 2026? (Above 2.4%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy increases by more than 2.4% in the twelve months ending September 2026 (as represented by the one-decimal place value reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics), then the market resolves to Yes.
In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI News Release, August 2026)
recent_facts.fact: Core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 0.3% seasonally adjusted in August 2026 and 2.4% over the 12 months ending August, not seasonally adjusted. The NSA core index was 338.041 in August 2026 and 329.970 in August 2025, so the unrounded year-over-year rate is about 2.446%.

recent_facts.source: Derived from BLS index levels (BLS release; Ball State CBER for Sep 2025)
recent_facts.fact: Ball State's CBER lists the September 2025 NSA core index as 330.54. This is a secondary source; confirm against BLS series CUUR0000SA0L1E. A one-decimal reading of 2.5% or higher (an unrounded rate of about 2.45%+) needs a September 2026 NSA index of about 338.64 or more. That is an NSA monthly rise of about 0.177% or more from August's 338.041.

recent_facts.source: Derived from BLS/Ball State CBER index levels
recent_facts.fact: The base month drops out of the 12-month window. The NSA core index rose from 329.970 in August 2025 to about 330.54 in September 2025, roughly +0.17%. So if the September 2026 NSA monthly gain is above about 0.18%, the 12-month rate rises from 2.446% toward 2.45% or more. If the gain is below that, the rate stays at or below 2.4% rounded.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (September 2025 CPI release, archived)
recent_facts.fact: In September 2025, core CPI rose 0.2% seasonally adjusted (after +0.3% in each of July and August 2025). The 12-month core rate was 3.0%.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI News Release, August 2026)
recent_facts.fact: Recent seasonally adjusted monthly core CPI changes for 2026: March +0.2%, April +0.4%, May +0.2%, June 0.0%, July +0.2%, August +0.3%. Shelter rose 0.3% in August after 0.1% in July.

The 12-month core rate eased to 2.4% in August from 2.5% in July 2026, described as the lowest since March 2021. Headline CPI was 3.4% year over year, with gasoline up 3.9% in August and 27.4% over the year.
BLS is scheduled to release the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. That is after the question's 12:25 UTC close time on the same day.
According to FOMC minutes reported on October 7, 2026, Fed officials saw inflation risks worsening before the Fed raised rates in September 2026. The next FOMC meeting is October 27-28.
Record September gasoline prices are pushing headline CPI up. Energy is not part of the core index, which excludes food and energy.

market.question: Will Gadi Eizenkot be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: An average of the last 10 polls, updated 8 Oct 2026, has Likud 23, Yashar (Eisenkot) 22, B'Yachad (Bennett–Lapid) 11 and The Democrats 9. Shas, UTJ, Otzma Yehudit, Yisrael Beiteinu and the Joint List have 8 each, RZP–Zehut 6 and Ra'am 5. Bloc totals: Netanyahu bloc 53, Change bloc 50, Arab parties 13. No bloc reaches the 61 needed for a majority.

Latest individual polls for Likud/Yashar/B'Yachad: Zman Yisrael 8 Oct 20/24/13; Direct Polls/i24 8 Oct 26/20/11; Channel 14 7 Oct 31/23/8; Channel 13 7 Oct 20/20/12; Channel 12 5 Oct 21/23/13; Kan 4 Oct 21/23/12.
A Channel 13 poll put Netanyahu's bloc at 55 seats and Eisenkot's bloc, without the Arab parties, at 50. Neither reaches 61 without the Arab parties.

A Maariv poll gave the Netanyahu bloc 51 seats and the opposition 53. Yashar had 21, Likud 19, Bennett's Together 13 and Otzma Yehudit 9. A Channel 14 poll from early October gave the right-wing bloc 63 seats, with Likud at 32.

The election is on 27 Oct 2026, and official results are due to be confirmed on 4 Nov 2026. The question closes on 28 Oct 2026, so no post-election prime minister can be sworn in before it closes. Netanyahu stays in office as caretaker until a new government is sworn in, and caretaker status does not count for resolution.

After results are certified, the president has 7 days for consultations, then gives one MK 28 days to form a government, extendable by up to 14 days. If that fails, the mandate can go to another MK or to the Knesset (which needs 61 MKs backing one candidate), or new elections are triggered.

Gantz (Blue and White) has ruled out backing a Netanyahu government. Eisenkot said he would work with junior right-wing partners only if Netanyahu is no longer PM. Ra'am says it wants to replace the Netanyahu government, and the Joint List (Hadash, Ta'al, Balad, merged in late August) said it would 'do more than' back an opposition candidate. The threshold is 3.25%, and Netanyahu has warned that small right-wing parties falling below it could cost the right its majority.

Joint tickets: Bennett 2026 and Yesh Atid run as 'Together', headed by Bennett. RZP and Zehut merged, approved 6 Sep. Tropper joined Yashar, and Hendel allied with Zelekha's New Economic Party. The Unity party dropped out on 4 Sep. A Likud–New Hope merger had not been approved by the Knesset House Committee as of July. 38 lists were submitted.

At his May 2026 campaign launch, Avigdor Liberman vowed not to sit in a government with Netanyahu. Bennett has announced a 'no Arab parties' position. I found no explicit pledge from Bennett ruling out Netanyahu (unverified).

Eisenkot challenged Netanyahu to a televised debate, and as of the latest reports Netanyahu had not responded. Likud's campaign attacks Eisenkot's possible reliance on Ra'am's Mansour Abbas, Tibi, Golan and Liberman.
Remaining dates: surplus-vote agreement deadline 16 Oct, voting at diplomatic missions 20 Oct, election 27 Oct, official results confirmed 4 Nov 2026.

In 2022 the final Times of Israel polling average gave Netanyahu's bloc 60.3 seats; it won 64. In the final week it passed 61 in 6 of 15 polls. The extra seats came mostly because Meretz and Balad fell below the threshold, wasting about 290,000 votes, even though the blocs were only about 30,000 votes apart.

Recent gaps between election and swearing-in (from memory, unverified): 2022, election 1 Nov, Netanyahu sworn in 29 Dec, about 58 days. 2021, election 23 Mar, Bennett sworn in 13 Jun, after Netanyahu's mandate expired unused. 2019–2020, three elections with no new government until May 2020.
A late-September poll had Eisenkot's Yashar and Likud tied, with Smotrich's list at a new high. A late-September Kan poll had each bloc at 52 seats, with Yashar 23 and Likud 21.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Iowa Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Iowa U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

market.question: Will Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by less than 4%?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $95 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.

recent_facts.fact: Lloyd's counted 290 Bab el-Mandeb transits for Sep 21–27 (preliminary), up from 264 the week before. Its four-week preliminary average was 280 per week, against 316 in June and 257 in January 2026. Lloyd's said Houthi threats have not derailed the return to the Red Sea.

The Houthi naval blockade on Saudi shipping took effect on 20 July 2026, and an attack in the week to 13 September halted crude exports from Yanbu. Ships are queuing for escorts because the EU's Operation Aspides does not have enough warships, according to Kaja Kallas.
In the second week of the Houthi blockade of Saudi Arabia, Bab el-Mandeb traffic was 38% below normal. In the week starting 20 July, transits fell to 269 from 354 in the week before the blockade.
On October 4, 2026, the products tanker Chrystal Sky (73,976 dwt) reported explosions about 60 nautical miles south of Mokha, Yemen.

A Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's airport on October 8, 2026 killed 3 people, and the Houthis warned of a long conflict. The Saudi-Houthi war is escalating, and the Houthis took stretches of the Red Sea coast along Bab el-Mandeb in September.

The Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi-linked shipping and have struck commercial vessels passing through Bab al-Mandab. On September 18, the UN Security Council condemned the attacks, and Saudi-backed government forces are running the 'Dawn of Yemen' counter-offensive.

market.question: Will Max Verstappen win the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix?
market.rules:
This is a polymarket on the winner of the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix, scheduled for Oct 11, 2026.

If the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix is canceled or rescheduled to a date after Oct 18, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other.”

This market will resolve in favor of the driver who is officially listed in first place in the Final Classification published by the FIA following the conclusion of the race. The Final Classification is typically released 30-60 minutes after the race ends and includes any applied time penalties and official adjustments.

Disqualifications or changes made after the publication of the Final Classification will not affect market resolution. The timing of the podium ceremony does not determine the result for this market — only the FIA's published classification will be used to resolve this market.

The resolution source will be the official Formula 1 website and a consensus of credible sports news reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Verstappen was fastest in Singapore sprint qualifying with 1:31.156. Russell was +0.120s, Leclerc +0.243, Piastri +0.298, Norris +0.431, Hamilton +0.546, championship leader Antonelli 7th at +0.693, and Verstappen's teammate Hadjar 9th at +1.791. This sets the grid for the sprint only. The Grand Prix grid comes from a separate qualifying session.

The FIA stewards are investigating Verstappen for passing Lewis Hamilton under yellow flags at Turn 7 in SQ1, after Perez crashed. A guilty finding could bring a sprint grid penalty. As of the latest reports found, no decision had been published.
Before SQ1, Red Bull changed Verstappen's ERS unit as a precaution over a suspected fault. He was still fastest in all three sprint qualifying segments.

In the only practice session (FP1), Verstappen was 6th, 0.732s behind Russell's 1:32.274, after radio problems and time stuck in the garage. Leclerc was 2nd and Norris 3rd. Reports said his medium-tyre pace was more than half a second faster than anyone else's on mediums.

In the previous round, Verstappen won the rain-delayed Bahrain GP, which was held at Sepang, Malaysia. He started from pole and finished 2.307s ahead of Antonelli, with Hamilton 3rd. It was his first win of 2026.
At the Azerbaijan GP, Verstappen finished 2nd, 0.196s behind winner George Russell, and Hadjar was 3rd. It was Russell's third win of 2026.

In 2026 Verstappen has 8 podiums and 1 win, and is 6th in the standings with 188 points, 132 behind Antonelli. In the 9 races since Austria he has 1 win, six 2nd- or 3rd-place finishes and 2 DNFs, an average finish of 2.14 excluding DNFs.

16 of the 23 rounds of 2026 are complete. Winners found include Antonelli (China, Canada, Belgium), Russell (Austria, Azerbaijan) and Verstappen (Bahrain at Sepang). Mercedes lead the constructors' standings with 538 points after Baku, ahead of Ferrari 378, McLaren 306 and Red Bull 263.
This is Singapore's first sprint weekend. The sprint and Grand Prix qualifying are still to come on Saturday, and the Grand Prix is on Sunday, October 11, 2026.

The Grand Prix pole-sitter has won all but 5 Singapore Grands Prix, roughly 11 of 16 through 2025. Russell won from pole in 2025. The count is inferred from the source's wording, so treat it as unverified.
Verstappen has never won the Singapore GP. Motorsport.com said this sprint qualifying result is his first fastest qualifying time of any kind at Marina Bay.

Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

recent_facts.fact: The Democratic nominee is former state Senate President Troy Jackson. He faces Republican incumbent Susan Collins. Wikipedia lists no independent candidates as having qualified: Tim Rich did not qualify and Phillip Rench withdrew. That suggests a two-candidate ballot, so a ranked-choice runoff is unlikely to matter.

Graham Platner won the June Democratic primary. He withdrew on July 10, 2026, after sexual assault accusations and other controversies. A Democratic nominating convention chose Troy Jackson to replace him on July 25, 2026.
Marist poll, Oct 1–4, 1,505 registered voters (±3.8%): Jackson 51%, Collins 47%, other 1%, undecided 1%.

Other polls ending around Oct 1, all likely voters: Trafalgar (R), 1,091 LV: 46–46 with 8% undecided. Wedgewood, 400 LV: Jackson 52, Collins 48. CBS News/YouGov, 1,136 LV: 50–50. co/efficient (R), Sep 28–30, 1,240 LV: Collins 48, Jackson 46, 6% undecided.

Late-September polls: Maine People's Resource Center (Sep 25–29): Jackson 49, Collins 47. InsiderAdvantage (R) (Sep 22–23): 46–46. Fabrizio Ward/Impact Research (Sep 20–22): Jackson 50, Collins 47. NYT/Siena (Sep 15–22, 619 LV): Collins 49, Jackson 46. UNH (Sep 17–21, 1,312 LV): Jackson 51, Collins 47.

Polling averages for Sep 20–Oct 4: 270toWin had Jackson 49.1%, Collins 47.6%. The average across aggregators was Jackson 48.8%, Collins 47.2%. RealClearPolling showed a near tie, Jackson 47.6% to Collins 47.5%.

Jackson led or tied Collins in every listed poll from mid-July to mid-September. Examples: UNH Jul 15–20, Jackson 49–46. Hart (D), Jackson 49–45. UMass/YouGov Aug 28–Sep 14, Jackson 48–43. Rasmussen (R), Sep 8–10, Jackson 46–45. Exceptions: the Abacus registered-voter version had Collins 46–45, and Quantus (Sep 14–15) had Collins 48–47.

In 2020, Democrat Sara Gideon led nearly every public poll and finished 6.5 points ahead in the RealClearPolitics average. Collins still won with just under 51% of the vote, a margin of roughly 8–9 points (about 8.6 by recollection, not verified from the sources). That puts the polling miss at about 15 points in Collins's favor.
Unverified recollection: Collins has won all 5 of her Senate general elections (1996, 2002, 2008, 2014, 2020).
Second debate (WMTW, Oct 8) was testy. Jackson accused Collins and her husband of profiting from the Iran war, without offering specific evidence. The two candidates accused each other of corruption.

About a week before Oct 8, ProPublica reported that the FBI sought to investigate bribery claims involving Collins, tied to $150,000 that convicted contractor Martin Kao says he routed to a pro-Collins super PAC. ProPublica says the probe was dropped after Trump returned to office. Collins's campaign calls the allegations recycled and says she was cleared. Jackson called it 'corruption of the highest order.'
As of June 30, 2026, Collins had raised $18.9M and had $11.0M cash on hand. Jackson was not yet a candidate then and shows $0. Trump has not endorsed Collins.
Two more debates are scheduled: Oct 13 (WABI/WAGM) and Oct 15 (News Center Maine/Portland Press Herald/Maine Public). Election day is November 3, 2026.

Maine uses ranked-choice voting for U.S. Senate races. The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Jackson, as the replacement Democratic nominee, counts as the Democrat.

market.question: Will the Federal Reserve Hike rates by 0bps at their October 2026 meeting? (Fed maintains rate)
market.rules:
If the Federal Reserve does a Hike of 0bps on October 28, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The outcomes are mutually exclusive: at most one can resolve to Yes. For example, a 50-basis-point hike resolves “Hike   25 bps” to Yes and “Hike 25 bps” to No.

If the scheduled FOMC meeting is canceled and does not occur on its scheduled date, “Fed maintains rate” resolves to Yes and all other outcomes resolve to No.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%. This was its first hike since 2023.
The next FOMC meeting is October 27–28, 2026, with the decision on October 28. The meeting after that is December 8–9, 2026.

The September minutes, released October 7, said 'most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end.' They gave no timing and said future decisions depend on incoming information.

In an October 1 speech, Vice Chair Jefferson said policymakers 'will need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time' before deciding on another increase. He also said inflation risks are tilted to the upside.

In separate speeches, Jefferson and New York Fed President Williams said the Fed has time to assess the economy before considering another hike. Williams said there was 'no need for urgency' and 'we have time to gather more information.'
On September 24, Williams said it is 'reasonable' to expect another rate hike by the end of the year.
Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said more hikes lie ahead. Dallas Fed President Logan has said at least two more increases may be needed.
At the July 2026 meeting the Fed held rates, but three FOMC members dissented in favor of a 25 bp hike.

September nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000–90,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%. July was revised to -10,000 and August to +133,000. Average hourly earnings rose 0.1% in the month and 3.0% over 12 months.

August PCE inflation was 3.4% headline and 3.0% core, both below expectations. August CPI rose 0.4% for the month and 3.4% year over year. Consumers' median 12-month inflation expectation rose to 3.9%.
The September 2026 CPI is due Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the October 27–28 meeting. The October CPI is due November 10, after the meeting.
At Jackson Hole, Chair Warsh said inflation is too high and 'we have work to do.' He has said he intends to give less forward guidance.

'Fed maintains rate' resolves Yes if the target range is unchanged on October 28, or if the meeting is canceled. 'Hike 25bps' resolves Yes only for an increase of exactly 25 bps, which would take the range to 4.00%-4.25%.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 15–16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted unanimously, 12-0, to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%–4.00%. That makes 4.00% the upper bound going into the October meeting, and it was the Fed's first hike since 2023.
The Board raised the interest rate on reserve balances to 3.90%, effective September 17, 2026, and raised the primary credit rate to 4.00%.

In the September dot plot the median participant projected one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at about 4.1%, then no change in 2027. According to CNBC, 16 of 18 participants projected one more hike this year and 4 projected two. The two meetings left in 2026 are October and December.

The September minutes, released October 7, show officials were worried that inflation pressures could spread. Most participants thought another hike by year-end would likely be appropriate. The minutes did not commit to October specifically.
The September jobs report was weak. Payrolls rose only 29,000, below estimates of more than 80,000, and unemployment edged up to 4.2%. July was revised down by 31,000 jobs and August by 29,000.

The August PCE report showed core prices up 3.0% year over year, below the 3.3% consensus. Inflation was still described as elevated because of energy prices from the Iran war and AI-related price pressures.

On September 29, New York Fed President John Williams said one more rate increase by the end of this year could be appropriate but there was no need to rush. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said reaching a judgment on further adjustments could take more time.
Chair Kevin Warsh has given little guidance on the next move since the September meeting. At his September press conference he said 'Inflation is too high and has been for too long.'
The September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the FOMC meeting. One low-quality source claims BLS data releases may be disrupted; this is unverified.
The FOMC meets October 27–28, 2026 and the statement is due October 28. The October jobs report will not come out until early November, after the meeting.

The question resolves on the change in the upper bound (currently 4.00%) according to the October 28 FOMC statement. If no statement is released, it resolves to 'No change'. Any non-25 bp move is rounded up to the nearest 25 bp.

recent_facts.fact: The all-items CPI-U rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted) in the 12 months ending August 2026, the same rate as for the 12 months ending July. The NSA index level for August 2026 was 334.980 (1982-84=100).

The September 2025 NSA CPI-U index was 324.800, and the August 2025 index was about 323.976. That makes the September 2025 month-over-month NSA change about +0.25%, and this month drops out of the year-over-year base. market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: An average of the last 10 polls, updated 8 Oct 2026, has Likud 23, Yashar (Eisenkot) 22, B'Yachad (Bennett–Lapid) 11 and The Democrats 9. Shas, UTJ, Otzma Yehudit, Yisrael Beiteinu and the Joint List have 8 each, RZP–Zehut 6 and Ra'am 5. Bloc totals: Netanyahu bloc 53, Change bloc 50, Arab parties 13. No bloc reaches the 61 needed for a majority.

Latest individual polls for Likud/Yashar/B'Yachad: Zman Yisrael 8 Oct 20/24/13; Direct Polls/i24 8 Oct 26/20/11; Channel 14 7 Oct 31/23/8; Channel 13 7 Oct 20/20/12; Channel 12 5 Oct 21/23/13; Kan 4 Oct 21/23/12.
A Channel 13 poll put Netanyahu's bloc at 55 seats and Eisenkot's bloc, without the Arab parties, at 50. Neither reaches 61 without the Arab parties.

A Maariv poll gave the Netanyahu bloc 51 seats and the opposition 53. Yashar had 21, Likud 19, Bennett's Together 13 and Otzma Yehudit 9. A Channel 14 poll from early October gave the right-wing bloc 63 seats, with Likud at 32.

The election is on 27 Oct 2026, and official results are due to be confirmed on 4 Nov 2026. The question closes on 28 Oct 2026, so no post-election prime minister can be sworn in before it closes. Netanyahu stays in office as caretaker until a new government is sworn in, and caretaker status does not count for resolution.

After results are certified, the president has 7 days for consultations, then gives one MK 28 days to form a government, extendable by up to 14 days. If that fails, the mandate can go to another MK or to the Knesset (which needs 61 MKs backing one candidate), or new elections are triggered.

Gantz (Blue and White) has ruled out backing a Netanyahu government. Eisenkot said he would work with junior right-wing partners only if Netanyahu is no longer PM. Ra'am says it wants to replace the Netanyahu government, and the Joint List (Hadash, Ta'al, Balad, merged in late August) said it would 'do more than' back an opposition candidate. The threshold is 3.25%, and Netanyahu has warned that small right-wing parties falling below it could cost the right its majority.

Joint tickets: Bennett 2026 and Yesh Atid run as 'Together', headed by Bennett. RZP and Zehut merged, approved 6 Sep. Tropper joined Yashar, and Hendel allied with Zelekha's New Economic Party. The Unity party dropped out on 4 Sep. A Likud–New Hope merger had not been approved by the Knesset House Committee as of July. 38 lists were submitted.

At his May 2026 campaign launch, Avigdor Liberman vowed not to sit in a government with Netanyahu. Bennett has announced a 'no Arab parties' position. I found no explicit pledge from Bennett ruling out Netanyahu (unverified).

Eisenkot challenged Netanyahu to a televised debate, and as of the latest reports Netanyahu had not responded. Likud's campaign attacks Eisenkot's possible reliance on Ra'am's Mansour Abbas, Tibi, Golan and Liberman.
Remaining dates: surplus-vote agreement deadline 16 Oct, voting at diplomatic missions 20 Oct, election 27 Oct, official results confirmed 4 Nov 2026.

In 2022 the final Times of Israel polling average gave Netanyahu's bloc 60.3 seats; it won 64. In the final week it passed 61 in 6 of 15 polls. The extra seats came mostly because Meretz and Balad fell below the threshold, wasting about 290,000 votes, even though the blocs were only about 30,000 votes apart.

Recent gaps between election and swearing-in (from memory, unverified): 2022, election 1 Nov, Netanyahu sworn in 29 Dec, about 58 days. 2021, election 23 Mar, Bennett sworn in 13 Jun, after Netanyahu's mandate expired unused. 2019–2020, three elections with no new government until May 2020.
A late-September poll had Eisenkot's Yashar and Likud tied, with Smotrich's list at a new high. A late-September Kan poll had each bloc at 52 seats, with Yashar 23 and Likud 21.

(see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

AP reports that if his party wins a majority of seats, parliament is expected to elect him prime minister. He launched his campaign at a packed Belgrade arena on 3 October.

Vučić heads list no. 1, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led, 209,130 signatures), as SNS's candidate for Prime Minister. All 250 seats are up and 126 are needed for a majority. Seats are allocated by d'Hondt in one nationwide constituency with a 3% threshold, and minority parties are exempt from the threshold.

Faktor Plus poll, 16–20 Sept, n=986: United Serbia 48.6% (+1.4), Student List 37.1% (+5.6), SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, NADA 2.8%. Stated willingness to vote was 62%. Faktor Plus is described as pro-government-leaning. I found no October poll or independent poll.
The page says the SNS–Student List race has tightened. Some polls put SNS first and others put the Student List first. It gives no poll figures in its text.

The People's Serbia coalition withdrew its list on 22 September to back the Student List (list no. 3, ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović). Faktor Plus also said the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn, which consolidated the opposition vote.

Other lists: 'Factor of Stability!' led by Ivica Dačić (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni), which is the ruling coalition's traditional partner; European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš, SSP and SRCE); Authentic Right (NADA). Fifteen other lists, including minority lists, were also submitted.

In the 2024 cycle, parliament had one month to constitute itself after final results, then 90 days to form a government. The president nominates the PM-designate, who presents a programme and cabinet for an Assembly vote. If no government is elected in time, parliament is dissolved and new elections are called.

The question closes on 25 October 2026, election day. Any Assembly vote electing a new prime minister would come after the new parliament's constitutive session, about 30 days after final results, so it would fall after the close date. The resolution window runs to 30 June 2028.
In 2022, SNS took about 43% and roughly 120 seats. It stayed the largest party but lost its outright majority (126). It still formed a government with partners.

In 2020, the SNS-led 'For Our Children' coalition won 188 of 250 seats, a two-thirds majority, in a vote boycotted by most opposition parties. In 2016, SNS won 131 seats. SNS-led lists have finished first in every parliamentary election from 2014 to 2023. 2012 is not verified here.

This election follows about two years of student-led protests that began after the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station disaster, with more than 100,000 people protesting at the March 2025 peak. Vučić previously served as Serbia's prime minister from 2014 to 2017, before becoming president.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: FiftyPlusOne's generic ballot average dated October 7, 2026 has Democrats at 51.2% and Republicans at 43.4%, a lead of about D+8.

Cook's House ratings: 185 Solid D, 12 Likely D, 11 Lean D (208 total leaning D), 22 Toss Up, 10 Lean R, 19 Likely R, 176 Solid R (205 total leaning R). Republicans hold 17 of the 22 toss-ups and Democrats hold 5. A majority takes 218 seats. These figures come from a search summary because the page itself returned a 403 error.
Cook's September 25, 2026 update moved 15 House race ratings toward Democrats.

The Iran war began in late February 2026. Net support for it is -27.9 (32.1% support, 60.0% oppose), the worst since it started. AAA regular gasoline averages $4.36 a gallon. The September jobs report showed +29,000 jobs with 60,000 in downward revisions, and unemployment rose to 4.2%.
The analysis says Republican-favoring redistricting means Democrats need to win the national House vote by about 3–4 points to win a House majority.
After ten states redrew their maps for 2026, Cook says the median House seat now has a Cook PVI of R+3. It calls the map more Republican-skewed and less elastic than before. (Date approximate.)

recent_facts.source: AP via Washington Examiner / Jim Ellis (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: AP estimated Republicans could net about 10 House seats from redistricting if the new maps perform as designed (new maps in TX, MO, NC, OH, FL, TN, LA, AL, offset by Democratic gains in CA and UT). Jim Ellis put the Republican net gain at 8–12 seats after Virginia's Supreme Court struck down the Democratic map, which leaves Virginia's 6D-5R map in place. The date is approximate; I could not confirm the final status of the Florida, Louisiana and Alabama maps.
Olsen's analysis says a D+8.3 generic ballot corresponds to Democrats winning about 225 districts.

NPR reports that Cook lists 43 competitive districts, 22 of them toss-ups. Toss-ups include races in AZ, CA, CO, FL, IA, MI, NY, OH, PA, TX, VA and WI. Axios (September 25) reported House Republicans as 'on track to lose majority.'
Republicans won the House 220–215 in 2024. The current House is reported at 218 Republicans to 214 Democrats.

recent_facts.source: Gallup / secondary commentary (unverified against primary data)
recent_facts.fact: In 18 of the 20 midterms from 1946 to 2022, the president's party lost House seats; the exceptions were 1998 and 2002. When the president's approval was under 50%, his party lost an average of 37 House seats, compared with 14 when approval was over 50%.

Election day is November 3, 2026, and all 435 House seats are on the ballot. Both questions close on 2026-11-04 at 04:59 UTC, which is the night of the election, before many close races will have been called.
